text:
Maya (PM): Quick sync — customer is requesting a private-beta with HSM-backed keys + <100ms p95 latency for short-chat flows. Can we sketch dependencies and a minimal rollout path?

Raj (EngRuntime): Short answer: doable but needs a dedicated runtime variant (quant+KV cache tuned) and a pre-warmed GPU pool. Estimate: 2 engs x 4w to add the runtime knobs + test harness.

Ben (Infra): We can carve dedicated capacity in Dedicated for the beta. Need to know expected qps and burst profile. Also, will this require VPC peering + subnet edits?

Maya (PM): Good Qs — customer expects ~60 rps peak, mostly short (16–64 tokens). They'll want private control plane and VPC.

Leah (Security): HSM path: decision point — customer-managed KMS (BYOK) or Redwood-managed KMS with HW-backed keys. BYOK adds onboarding time (certs + audit). Also need threat model and export controls check.

Nina (DevEx): I'll own the onboarding checklist + runbook docs. Need a short prompt suite for quality regression checks and an example Terraform/VPC snippet.

Omar (SRE): Oncall impact: this adds a new runbook and an escalations flow to EngRuntime and Infra. If we do dedicated capacity, we should reserve a warm standby to avoid cold-start flakiness during beta.

Raj (EngRuntime): For latency: KV cache + aggressive prefix caching should get us sub-100ms p95 for those token sizes, provided batch sizes stay small. Will need canary tests in staging with the customer's prompt set.

Ben (Infra): I'll need a ticket with exact network CIDRs and an SLA for capacity commit. Also propose a 2-stage rollout: staging private tenant -> limited beta (2 customers) -> wider private GA. Canary policy: 5% traffic then 25%.

Leah (Security): Action: I'll run the HSM/BYOK risk assessment. Timeline: 3w for BYOK onboarding + audit, 1w for Redwood-managed KMS review. Which path do they prefer?

Maya (PM): I'll confirm tonight with the customer re: BYOK vs Redwood KMS. Rollout acceptance criteria I propose: 1) p95 latency <150ms on staging, 2) threat-model signoff, 3) successful canary with their prompt set, 4) DR doc + oncall rota.

Raj (EngRuntime): A note on engineering work: split into (A) runtime perf/kv caching (B) compatibility w/ HSM-backed key unwrap (C) canary harness. We can parallelize A+B if Infra gives env.

Ben (Infra): I'll open INF-5483 to reserve capacity and create the VPC stub.

DeployBot: INF-5483 created by Ben — capacity reservation + env stub assigned.

Leah (Security): ack. I'll link the risk assessment to INF-5483 once ready.

Nina (DevEx): I'll draft the onboarding doc and the minimal quickstart in the repo -> PR for review by EOD Friday.

Omar (SRE): Adding SRE to the canary checklist. Need to know rollback criteria (latency degradation >20% or error rate >0.5%).

Maya (PM): Thanks — next steps: I confirm KMS preference, Ben kicks off INF-5483, Raj and Ben align on env access, Leah starts assessment. Can everyone react with :thumbsup: if they can deliver the items within the timelines above?

Raj (EngRuntime): :thumbsup:

Ben (Infra): :thumbsup:

Leah (Security): :thumbsup:

Nina (DevEx): :thumbsup:

Omar (SRE): :thumbsup:

Maya (PM): Great — I'll post the customer's confirmation here when I have it and update the rollout criteria. Thanks all.
